transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-07-21 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~55m | Location: Zoom
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Lucas Rivera (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Quanta CTO), Priya Nair (Quanta ML), Sam Ortiz (Quanta Platform), Ellen Park (Quanta Security)

[00:00] Alex Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro, i'm alex from redwood — i'll run the session, maya and lucas are on the technical side. jordan, priya, sam, ellen — thanks for time. main goal today is parity mapping from what you run on openai/anthropic/together to our api and to show the console and optimize suggestions.

[00:22] Jordan Lee: yep, thanks. to set context — we have prod features using openai chat+embeds, and a small research path on anthropic for safety experiments. cost and tail latency are creeping up; platform wants options for dedicated capacity and stricter key management.

[00:40] Maya Patel: great, that's what we'll focus on. quick agenda: api parity (calls + streaming), embeddings mapping, console walkthrough incl. optimize suggestions, and then discuss pilot plan. sound good?

[01:05] Priya Nair: yep. one immediate question: for embeddings, together has a 1536-d model we use — how do we map to redwood embeddings, and what about vector store changes?

[01:20] Maya Patel: good call. redwood provides a model catalog — we have curated embeddings at 1536 and 768 dims depending on model family. quality-wise we do a small eval mapping: you can either match dimension for drop-in or reindex with 768 and get lower cost; our optimize tool will show expected recall differences and recommended quantization.

[01:45] Sam Ortiz: reindexing is nontrivial for us, long-running job. is there an in-place fallback for dual-indexing?

[01:55] Lucas Rivera: yes — we often recommend a phased approach: run a backfilled job on a copy then switch traffic. we also support prefix-based KV caching for prompt reuse which can mitigate cost while you reindex.

[02:15] Ellen Park: on security — can you confirm KMS integration, customer-managed keys, and audit logs? we need exportable logs for SOC2.

[02:28] Maya Patel: absolutely. redwood private supports customer KMS/HSM. hosted api has envelope encryption options and audit logs surfaced in the console; for enterprise/private we can enable full-blown HSM integration. i'll share the SOC2 + KMS docs after the call.

[02:45] Jordan Lee: another thing — function calling. our app relies heavily on structured function outputs. how compatible are your function-calling semantics with openai's?

[03:00] Alex Chen: we support function/tool calling and structured output. the semantics are very similar: you pass function schema, model returns args JSON. there are subtle differences in error codes and streaming encoding, but we provide example SDKs and a translation layer — you can swap with minimal changes. i'll drop sample curl and sdk snippets in the parity sheet.

[03:30] Priya Nair: latency expectations — our p95 for chat must be under 350ms for short prompts. what's typical on hosted and dedicated?

[03:45] Lucas Rivera: for hosted, p95 for typical chat on our medium family is around 250–400ms depending on length; dedicated GPUs can trim that to 120–220ms for short contexts. but depends on model, seq length, and batching. for micro-latency workloads we advise dedicated + smaller batch sizes and KV caching.

[04:10] Jordan Lee: curious about cost math — we pay per token on openai; are we moving to a different model?

[04:22] Maya Patel: hosted is still usage-based per-token/embedding. dedicated is reserved capacity — commit model; you get predictable throughput and lower unit costs. optimize tool will simulate token-level cost given your workload, showing tradeoffs for quantization and batch sizes.

[04:50] Sam Ortiz: about continuity — if we have a failover from dedicated to hosted, will model outputs be deterministic enough, or will there be drift?

[05:05] Lucas Rivera: model parity uses pinned model versions and variant mapping. drift is possible when switching model families; we ask customers to pin to verified variants. the console supports rollout policies: canary, A/B, automatic fallback to close variants. we'll show the rollout UI in a bit.

[05:30] Alex Chen: quick demo — switching to screen share to the console.

[05:50] [screen share starts] Maya Patel: here's the model catalog — you can filter by family, latency profile, and verified benchmarks. if i open the 'parity helper' we have a pre-baked mapping sheet that maps common OpenAI/Anthropic/Together endpoints to recommended redwood variants and notes on tokenization differences.

[06:20] Priya Nair: can we see an example for openai gpt-4o -> redwood medium-l?

[06:30] Maya Patel: yes — the sheet recommends medium-l or medium-l-8q depending on precision. for chat tokens, we show an estimated token delta due to tokenizer differences. there's also a recommended quantization profile for cost.

[07:05] Sam Ortiz: about streaming — our frontend uses streaming chunks to render partial outputs, would integration be straightforward?

[07:20] Lucas Rivera: we support streaming via server-sent events and websockets; the chunk framing has a slightly different metadata header but we have middleware examples for node/python that keep your client code unchanged.

[07:45] Jordan Lee: demo request — can we run a quick parity example? take an existing openai prompt and call redwood and compare tokens/latency?

[08:01] Alex Chen: yes — priya, did you paste that sample prompt earlier?

[08:10] Priya Nair: yes i put a short Q&A prompt in the shared doc.

[08:18] Maya Patel: running a live request now — calling redwood's chat endpoint with the same role messages.

[08:40] [console logs scroll]

[08:52] Maya Patel: result returned in 180ms p50, 210ms p95 on this test using medium-s. token spend shown here — 220 input, 480 output; our tokenization split differs by ~6% from your openai baseline where we saw 240/460 in your earlier run.

[09:15] Priya Nair: interesting — output quality looks comparable for this prompt. we'll need broader evals but good start.

[09:30] Jordan Lee: what's the suggested path to validate at scale? we have a few thousand daily active queries on this flow.

[09:45] Lucas Rivera: recommend a three-phase pilot: 1) bench with your representative prompt set in hosted for direct parity metrics, 2) run a short dedicated pilot with a small pool (1–2 GPUs) to measure tail latency and throughput and 3) a canary internal rollout syncing with your traffic router. we can automate step 1 and produce a report.

[10:10] Priya Nair: ok, for the benchmark we need to include our function-call heavy examples and embedding recall tests. can the perf harness do embeddings too?

[10:25] Maya Patel: yes, our benchmark harness supports text-gen, function calls, and embeddings workflows. it outputs recall/precision for embedding nearest-neighbor tests, and latency/cost breakdown. we'll need your prompt set and a small holdout eval set.

[10:40] Ellen Park: reiterating security — if we move to dedicated, will logs stay in our VPC and how long are audit logs retained?

[10:55] Lucas Rivera: with private/dedicated we can ship logs to your splunk/s3 bucket inside your VPC, retention is configurable. i'll coordinate with your security team on retention policy and redaction.

[11:10] Jordan Lee: are there any gotchas we should know about when porting from anthropic safety filters?

[11:20] Maya Patel: safety behaviors vary; we recommend running toxicity and safety eval sets during parity. our optimize tool can flag quality regressions tied to prompt sets and surface recommended model variants or prompt-engineering tweaks.

[11:40] Priya Nair: side note on embeddings dimensional mismatch — if we keep the original 1536 vectors, is there a quantized option to reduce storage?

[11:55] Lucas Rivera: yes — we have quantized storage options and recommend 8-bit quantization for vectors in many cases; optimize will project recall loss.

[12:10] Alex Chen: ok wrapping to next steps — we'll share the parity mapping sheet and sample code, maya will share SOC2/KMS docs, lucas will scope the dedicated pilot infra. priya will upload your prompt set and eval holdout.

[12:30] Jordan Lee: timeline — we aim to start the bench next week and have a pilot in the week after. is that realistic?

[12:40] Maya Patel: yes — if we get prompts and access by 7/22 we can kick off hosted bench the week of 7/28 and spin up dedicated pilot the following week.

[12:55] Priya Nair: one operational question — how are credentials rotated and do we get event hooks when model versions change?

[13:05] Lucas Rivera: credentials can be short-lived tokens with rotation integrated into your vault; model version changes are protected behind rollouts and we emit events/traces via webhooks and tracing hooks in the console.

[13:25] Ellen Park: also checking compliance: do you support SAML SSO and RBAC with fine-grained roles?

[13:35] Maya Patel: yes, SAML/SCIM, RBAC and audit trails are standard on enterprise/private. we'll include the admin console screenshots in the deck.

[13:50] Alex Chen: cool — any other questions?

[13:58] Jordan Lee: not right now. we'll collect a couple more example prompts and send them to maya/priya.

[14:10] Alex Chen: great, thanks everyone. quick recap in chat: alex shares parity spreadsheet and sample SDKs; maya shares security docs; lucas will tee up pilot infra; priya sends prompt set. follow-ups targeted this week.

[14:30] Meeting end.

Notes about transcript: some names/accents garbled by auto-transcribe, occasional words merged (e.g., 'kvcache' -> 'k vacash'). speaker labels are correct for the most part; there are short gaps where two people speak over each other.
